description: deixis N[T] embedding vectors — the direct embedding E : L[T] → N[T] of ADR 0009 §10.1 and its partial inverse. E(Leaf(t)) = Node(Some(t), {}); E(Struct(m)) = Node(None, {k ↦ E(m[k])}); the inverse is defined exactly on trees whose valued positions are terminal. Hand-authored from docs/design/0009-optional-node-values.md alone, per vectors/NODE-PLAN.md; not generated by an implementation, and replayed against the four cores by tools/conformance/harness.mjs. Old-model trees use the spelling of vectors/README.md ({leaf} / {struct}), new-model trees the N[T] spelling of NODE-PLAN.md. The single `embedded-identity` case is a law BY REFERENCE over vectors/identity.json: its judgments are that file's, already reviewed, not new ones. Under ADR 0010 this file reads as the explicit optional instantiation Node[Option[fixture]], with the tag-respecting option slot of vectors/MNODE-PLAN.md; every case here holds there under the mandatory core's generic laws (checked case by case on 2026-09-23; see NODE-PLAN.md).

cases.name: embed-empty-struct
cases.note: X12. E(Struct({})) = Node(None, {}), the single unvalued node e (§4 correspondence).

cases.name: embed-leaf-with-empty-payload-is-some-not-none
cases.note: X3/X12. A leaf holding an empty payload embeds as Some(empty). Mapping it to None would merge it with the empty struct, and identity.json's empty-leaf-is-not-the-empty-struct forbids that.

cases.name: embed-struct-with-leaf-empty-key-and-empty-struct-children
cases.note: X12/X5. Keys carry over exactly, the empty key included; E applies pointwise to children (D_E(n) = D_n, v_E(n) = v_n).

cases.name: embed-nested
cases.note: X12. E(at(n,p)) ≡ at(E(n),p): every interior node is unvalued, and the only value is at the leaf path.

cases.name: unembed-valued-childless-is-a-leaf
cases.note: §10.1: the inverse is defined on trees with terminal valued positions.

cases.name: unembed-unvalued-with-leaf-child
cases.note: §10.1. All valued positions are terminal, so the tree is in E's image.

cases.name: unembed-valued-node-with-children-is-undefined
cases.note: §10.1: a valued position with a descendant has no L preimage. This is exactly the tree node-attach.json's attach-at-valued-root produces from E(Leaf(7)), so it also shows that E's image is not closed under attachment.

cases.name: unembed-deep-valued-interior-is-undefined
cases.note: §10.1 below the root. A partial unembedding that drops the value at 6b, or drops its child, would invent an L preimage.

cases.name: embedding-preserves-and-reflects-identity-over-identity-json
cases.law: for every case of the source: E(left) ≡ E(right) in N iff the case's `equal` is true
cases.note: X12. §10.1: n ≡ m iff E(n) ≡ E(m). The verdicts are identity.json's, which were reviewed as old-model judgments. This case adds none of its own and re-reads all 21 through E, so the embedding claim is tested on judgments that existed before ADR 0009. A replayer MUST refuse if the source's counts differ from the three pinned here. Such a change is an erratum to identity.json, and this law must then be re-checked by a person, not silently re-run.
